revision.section_line: College, high school, and Canadian football

section_college.heading: ===College, high school, and Canadian football===
section_college.scope_sentence: In [[college football|college]] (since the [[1996 NCAA Division I-A football season|1996 season]]) and [[high school football]], as well as the [[Canadian Football League]] (since the 2000 season) and the short-lived [[Alliance of American Football]], an ''overtime procedure'' is used to determine the winner.
section_college.repeat_sentence: If the score remains tied at the end of the first overtime period, the procedure is repeated.
section_college.until_winner_sentence: In American college and high school football, the overtime periods are continued until a winner is determined.
section_college.ncaa_two_point_sentence: In [[College football|NCAA football]], since 2021, teams must attempt a [[two-point conversion]] after a touchdown in double overtime; all overtime procedures thereafter consist of two-point conversion attempts and are scored as such.
section_college.points_count_sentence: All points scored in overtime count as if they were scored in regulation.
section_college.contrast_cfl_sentence: Before 2026, the CFL limited overtime procedures to two in regular-season games; if the scores were still level, the game was a tie.
section_college.contrast_note: the same section names the leagues whose overtime CAN end level (the CFL before 2026, the AAF's regular season); it names no such limit for college football
